annotation.label: C minor governs; no secure modulation
annotation.body: The opening C–E-flat–G sonority and repeated G dominants with B-natural resolving to C minor establish C minor rather than E-flat major. The final C-minor sonority confirms that center. Chromatic excursions do not establish a lasting replacement tonic.

annotation.label: Local authentic arrival
annotation.body: G bass and B-natural support dominant harmony, completed by D–F at 11/16, before C minor arrives at 3/4. E-flat is uppermost at the arrival, making this an imperfect-authentic-type gesture rather than decisive phrase closure.

annotation.label: Brief A-flat emphasis
annotation.body: A-flat–D-flat–E-flat7–A-flat in measure 2 gives the submediant a local tonic-like role. Measure 3 immediately restores G7 directed toward C, so this is a brief tonicization, not a secure modulation to A-flat.

annotation.label: Applied dominants, then G tonicization
annotation.body: C7 with E-natural and B-flat in measure 3 points toward F minor, followed by a return to C minor. Measure 4 then twice moves from D7, with F-sharp, to G major with B-natural. This clearly tonicizes G, but subsequent C-minor material prevents a secure reading of lasting modulation.

annotation.label: Local cadential arrival on G
annotation.body: The second D7–G motion ends with root-position G and uppermost G at 3/4, giving a local authentic-cadence effect in the tonicized dominant. In the larger C-minor context it can also sound like dominant punctuation; it does not alone prove modulation.

annotation.label: Continuation across the window edge
annotation.body: Measure 6 ends with G7 over F, which resolves to C minor over E-flat at measure 7's opening. Both chords are inverted, and the phrase continues through F minor and another dominant. This is a connective resolution, not a secure half cadence or a new phrase forced by the window boundary.

annotation.label: Preliminary arrival, then strong C-minor cadence
annotation.body: Measure 7 moves from G harmony over B-natural to root-position C minor with E-flat uppermost: a weaker authentic arrival. Measure 8 supplies stronger closure: D-flat major precedes G7, the upper E-flat moves to D-natural, and root-position C minor arrives at 3/4 with C uppermost, supporting a perfect authentic cadence.

annotation.label: Repeated dominant-directed excursion
annotation.body: Measures 9–10 repeat measures 5–6. F-sharp and the D–F-sharp–A-flat–C sonority in measure 10 intensify motion to G major, but G then acquires F in the bass and resolves to C minor over E-flat in measure 11. This supports renewed dominant tonicization, not an independent G key area.

annotation.label: Connective resolution, then weaker tonic arrival
annotation.body: G7/F at the end of measure 10 resolves to C minor/E-flat at measure 11's opening, continuing rather than closing the phrase. Later, G harmony over B-natural resolves to root-position C minor at 3/4 with E-flat uppermost, repeating measure 7's weaker authentic gesture.

annotation.label: Final authentic cadence and tonic extension
annotation.body: Measure 12 repeats measure 8's D-flat-major preparation and root-position G7–C-minor close. Upper D-natural resolves to C at 3/4 above bass G–C, supporting a perfect authentic cadence. Measure 13 sustains and revoices C minor for a full measure; it extends the achieved closure rather than supplying another dominant–tonic cadence.

summaries: The E-flat signature supplies E-flat, A-flat and B-flat unless explicitly altered. Measures 1–3 emphasize C minor and A-flat, with brief dominant-directed shifts. Measures 4–6 increasingly emphasize G through D7–G motion, but do not securely establish a lasting modulation. Measure 6 ends on G7, leaving the phrase open.

C minor becomes the clear tonal center despite the E-flat signature. Measures 7–8 and 11–12 lead through G dominants to C-minor arrivals; measure 13 prolongs the final tonic under a fermata. Measures 9–10 repeat the earlier chromatic excursion toward G without establishing a lasting modulation.
diagnostics: Unmarked pitches are interpreted using the supplied E-flat signature and written accidental carry.

Measure 5's third-beat harmony is ambiguous: B–D–A-flat suggests an incomplete diminished seventh; the brief F-sharp is treated as a chromatic approach to G rather than a separate established harmony.
Unmarked E and A are E-flat and A-flat under the supplied signature.
The sparse chromatic sonorities in measure 9 admit alternative functional readings; chord labels distinguish their actual pitch content from inferred dominant function.
